subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equations of the tangents to the hyperbola 3x² − 4y² = 12 which (i) are parallel to y = x − 7, (ii) are perpendicular to y = x − 7.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Inter Maths-2B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.66 — SAQ chapter 9 Hyperbola, answer 79.2, the second of the printed twin pair 79.1/79.2 and also repeated verbatim as the second sub-item of the Bullet Model Paper's Q15 (book p.109). On the same ★★ SSP page as 79.1. Printed appearances: AP 15,17 · TS 15,18. Two-column page, no printed mark tags — the 2+2 split is OURS, matching 79.1's split. No error found in the book's printed working for this twin: unlike 79.1, neither slope here (1 or −1) coincides with an asymptote slope (±√3/2 ≈ ±0.87), so the tangent formula behaves normally and both parts give two genuine tangent lines each. Hyperbola is a SAQ+VSAQ-only unit on the book's IPE Blue Print (book p.5) — 4 marks in Section B (paper slot Q15) and 2 marks in Section A (paper slot Q5); it has NO LAQ chapter and no Section-C slot, so no 7-mark form is authored for this unit. insider_note: Unlike its twin question on this same page (79.1), neither slope here coincides with an asymptote slope, so both parts give two genuine, non-degenerate tangent lines — a useful contrast to point out to a student who has just met the degenerate case.

steps.label: Set up the tangent formula
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own — every result below substitutes into this formula.
steps.memory_tip: As always, read the hyperbola's a², b² off the standard form, then read the given line's own slope directly off its y = mx + c form.
lines: Divide by 12: x²/4 − y²/3 = 1 ⇒ a² = 4, b² = 3
Tangent with slope m: y = mx ± √(a²m² − b²)
Slope of the given line y = x − 7 is m = 1
steps.why: As before, read the hyperbola's a², b² off the standard form, then read the given line's own slope directly off its y = mx + c form.
common_mistakes: Using 3 and 4 as a² and b² directly from the given equation, without dividing by 12 first.
Missing that y = x − 7 is already in slope-intercept form, so its slope is simply the coefficient of x.

steps.label: Parallel tangent
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Slope 1 is not an asymptote slope here.
steps.memory_tip: The asymptotes of this hyperbola have slope ±√3/2 ≈ ±0.87 — nowhere near 1, so this case is straightforward.
lines: Parallel tangent has the same slope m = 1
steps.why: Slope 1 is not an asymptote slope here (the asymptotes have slope ±√3/2), so the formula gives two genuine parallel tangent lines, one on each side of the hyperbola.
common_mistakes: Writing only one of the two tangent lines instead of both signs of ±1.
Rearranging y = x + 1 incorrectly, e.g. as x + y − 1 = 0 instead of x − y + 1 = 0.

steps.label: Perpendicular tangent
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Slope −1 is likewise not an asymptote slope.
steps.memory_tip: The negative reciprocal of 1 is −1 — do not leave it as +1.
lines: Slope of the perpendicular is the negative
steps.why: The perpendicular slope −1 is likewise not an asymptote slope, so both tangent lines from this family are genuine.
common_mistakes: Taking the reciprocal of 1 as 1 instead of the NEGATIVE reciprocal −1.
Sign-slipping when moving −x ± 1 into general form.
